The Al-Al3Ni eutectic alloy has a eutectic temperature of 913 K and a eutectic composition of 2.9 at% Ni.
The Al3Ni intermetallic phase has an orthorhombic crystal structure with a common growth direction of [010].
In situ optical microscopy experiments were performed on thin Al-Al3Ni films with a slightly hypereutectic composition.

The optical microscopy experiments showed a transition from irregular, orientation-dependent eutectic growth at low velocities (< 1 μm/s) to more regular, coupled rod-like growth at higher velocities (up to 10 μm/s).
Ex situ FIB cross-sectioning and SEM analysis confirmed the transition from faceted to rounded Al3Ni crystals as the solidification velocity increased.
The calculated Jackson factor α for the Al3Ni-liquid interface is around 2.1, suggesting a mix of faceted and non-faceted character that can evolve with growth conditions.
The new synchrotron x-ray microscopy setup allowed for in situ observation of the solid-liquid interface dynamics and 3D characterization of the eutectic microstructure after solidification.
Hypereutectic Al-Ni alloy samples were found to contain blocky primary Al3Ni crystals in addition to the eutectic microstructure.
The researchers carefully selected and prepared micrometer-scale samples with the Al3Ni crystals aligned perpendicular to the x-ray beam for the synchrotron experiments.
Independent control of the upper and lower heating zones in the new synchrotron furnace allowed for the creation of a stable, tunable temperature gradient during directional solidification.
